Creates a new session (remote development environment) and starts provisioning it.

## Authentication

Accepts a Personal Access Token or a **Workspace API Token** (`bitwat_…`, created with Remote Dev Environments access). A PAT creates a personal session by default; set `owner_type` to `workspace` to create one owned by the workspace instead. A workspace token always creates **workspace-owned** sessions (`owner_type` may be omitted or `workspace`; `user` is rejected) — there is no user behind the token, so the session is visible to and manageable by every workspace member and listed under `?scope=SESSION_LIST_SCOPE_WORKSPACE`. The token can then manage the sessions it created — read, list, update, terminate, restore, delete, sweep terminated ones, run commands, transfer files, take screenshots — and read the workspace's templates and machine catalog; it never sees a member's personal session.

## Workspace-owned sessions

Use an existing template (`template_id`) or a bare `stack_id` + `machine_type`. Session inputs are given as plain values in `session_inputs`: every **required** input must be supplied that way, optional ones fall back to the template's `default_value` when omitted. Saved inputs are personal, so `saved_input_id` references and `map_saved_to_session_inputs` are rejected, and no saved SSH key or Claude credential is injected. `ai_prompt` is rejected for the same reason.

## Out of CPUs

When the workspace is out of CPUs for the session's machine family, or at its machine limit, the call is refused with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (HTTP 429) rather than a bad request. The error carries a `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` detail with `reason` `CPU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (metadata `family`, `quota_vcpu`, `used_vcpu`) or `MACHINE_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` (metadata `machine_limit`, `active_machines`), plus `action` (`create` or `restore`); the status message is written to be shown to a person as is.
